commit.message:
Preview AC adjustments from melded armour

Fixes #5470

Fix Gulch not showing up in "branches visited"

Fixes #5460

Break all constriction if walls interpose themselves

BVC and roots had LoS checks, but melee constriction did not (under the
assumption that you must have had LoS to be in melee range). However, it
was possible (if you had reaching constriction, such as via entangling or
aqua form) to have a wall appear in the attacker's way after the fact or
for them to be pushed around one, and constriction would still continue in
those cases. Now, it should not.

Don't list the max contam damage in the log when first contaminated

This information is still available in %, if the player wants it, but it
read as kind of stilted in the message log. (We don't point out exactly
how poisoned you are whenever something poisons you, after all.)

Don't give Sculpt Simulacrum to ghosts/player illusions

They can't actually cast it, but dummy code for an old version of the spell
still existed to a degree that allowed ghosts to be given it (without it
being clear to players that the spell did nothing).

Don't list Walk on Water as Beogh's capstone power

While you get it at the same piety as Blood for Blood, it's a less
impressive thing to list last (and the UI still doesn't actually say WHEN
you get any of this...)

Let Diminished Spells and Exposed trigger poltergeist trickster

They can't actually *apply* Exposed yet, but there will almost certainly be
some way in the future.

Fix stinger aux attack having much lower damage than intended (MrSquiggles)

At least if you didn't also have another tail-slap-granting mutation,
which green draconians fortunately did, but several other species capable
of getting this mutation did not.
Fix Sirocco no-hostile-in-range check
Cap assassin centipedes at +9 and reduce their paralysis chance a little

Let coglin assassin centipedes keep their name after leaving their body

If you're going to the trouble to name a weapon, you can surely also name
a pet.

Make coglins using a centipede bauble bypass their slow wielding trait

This was always intended, but for some reason the argument wasn't set in
one place.

(This also fixes a bug where you could create endless centipedes in your
inventory by using a buable while an enemy was in sight, and then
cancelling the wield when prompted by one interrupting you.)

Make weapon swapping after temporary weapons expire more robust

The previous system made bad assumptions when it came to characters
wielding multiple weapons, where it would try to swap back on whatever item
was in your main hand when you used a centipede bauble - regardless of
whether that was the one you unequipped or not.

Now we use a more thorough approach, assigning a unique identifier to the
weapon being swapped off, via a prop, and find the item again later by a
matching unique identifier.

(This is handled in a just slightly clunky way, but without any other cause
for a unique item ID at the moment, it felt heavy-handed to assign one to
every single item generated instead of doing it only on-demand when
equipping summoned items.)

Don't let Silence stop a lightning spire from firing

It's odd that it ever did, since the spell itself cannot be silenced. But
their custom targeting behavior bailed out while silenced anyway.

Don't blame the player for spike launcher kills of neutrals (rypofalem)

I debated whether it made more sense not to target them at all, but the
behavior by most proper independent allies is to still attack them, but not
blame the player for doing so. So this makes spike launcher follow similar
rules.

(Possibly we should make allies in general try not to attack pacified
creatures, but that is a much larger and more difficult change.)
Fix hypnogecko tail being hostile while worshipping Oka (dilly)

Make Indomitable description more general (particleface)

It's somewhat of a shame to lose the "This is how this happened" part of
the description in its most common case, but it's not only for North Wind
gale centaurs anymore (and I had always planned to use it in a couple other
future context, regardless).

Teleport lost jademantle crystals back to the player if they get stuck

While being extremely fast and wall-walking means these crystals rarely
get trapped away from the player for long, they can't actually move through
bushes or trees and so in some level configurations can get trapped
long-term behind such obstructions.

Instead, if they get more than 8 tiles away from the player, teleport them
back immediately.

Fix some side effects of slime merges

Resetting monsters (notably, merging slime creatures) was having
unexpected side effects:
* Charging revenant memories
* Working off temporary mutations
* Triggering the bane of succour

We fix the first two by folding "was not a reset" into gives_player_xp;
this doesn't affect other users but seems less surprising. Succour wants
different treatment because it deliberately triggers on summons, so we
directly check for reset kills there.

Fixes #5464

Translate mutation descriptions into Russian

Adds ru/mutations.txt, 265 entries that had no Russian at all. The file
covers ordinary mutations, demonspawn and Jiyva mutations, the fake
mutations used for forms, Ru sacrifices, Makhleb marks and banes.

The five Lua blocks are carried over structurally, with only their
strings translated, and all six $cmd[] references keep their markup so
the key shown matches the player's bindings.

Stat abbreviations follow what the game shows in its panels: AC, EV,
SH, MP and HP stay in Latin, as do Slay and Stealth+, while Strength,
Intelligence and Dexterity are translated because the English spells
them out too. School names follow the ones settled in dfda6708a4.

The stampede entry keeps its hand-made layout: the four winds are one
per line, with the literal newline escapes the English uses.
Fix spelling.
Fix typo.
Fix wording.
Fix typos.
Fix spacing.
Fix misnamed talismans.
Fix typos.
Allow draw_ring_animation to work with elemental colours
Properly describe the full reason a talisman is useless on xv

Allow oni to potion-cleave from drinking any potion

It's been a long-requested feature from more sources than I can remember
that oni be able to cleave from drinking moonshine - the flavor
associations are just too strong.

I considered carving out a specific exception for just moonshine, but with
Stalker now existing, it felt a shame that the potion-specialist species
had no synergy with the potion-specialist form. I considered making !mist
restore an extremely nominal amount of MP so that it would work with their
passive, but that felt a little forced.

Rather than carve out *two* exceptions, after some discussion with other
devs, I've decided to try allowing oni to cleave from any potion at all.
People felt this wouldn't be a significant buff in practice, but I am
conscious that it's a buff to one of the best-performing species we
currently have. But it's also a situational buff to the aspect of them that
is considered less strong, so perhaps it will be okay.

(I have given them a cautionary nerf of 1 to their polearm apt, since that
has the strongest synergy with all the extra potion cleaving.)

Don't make spellclaw/spellmotor attacks against unknown invisible targets

It gathered all targets in attack range, but this included unknown
monsters, potentially giving you unerring attacks against enemies the
player didn't even know about.

Instead, rely on known information. (You can still swing at invisible
things if you already know where they are.)

Allow Wanderers to start with the new talismans and bauble

The odds for some of these combinations are fairly arbitrary (and I'm not
sure if the logic for giving the casting forms is the best, since while
jademantle is only given if you have spells, there's no guarantee they
are *elemental* spells), but they can at least get these items now.

(Also, replace the chance of starting with Maw talisman with Spore
talisman; I forgot to adjust it when Maw was moved up a tier in 0.34.)
Update the manual for the new backgrounds
Don't break constriction on monsters when temp terrain beneath them reverts

Slightly tweak/simplify Globe of Annihilation explosion code

It would only print a message about the explosion being weak if its radius
was lower than the minimum possible in practice.

It looks like the code may have thought that distance == 1 meant that the
orb was hitting a non-adjacent target, but even if that was the case, I
don't see a reason to make the ability slightly weaker. Instead, just
treat it as always exploding to slightly simplify the code.

There should be no functional change besides messaging.

Slightly improve summon-dismissal effect of joining Okawaru

Okawaru attempts to dismisses all of the player's summoned allies when you
join them. However, it didn't check whether they were permitted allies or
not, nor whether it actually dismissed them before printing a message, and
would fail on anything without a summon timer.

This meant that it would remove things like foxfires, fail to remove
zombies, and sometimes even claim your summoned allies were dismissed when
nothing was (eg: for a permitted ally without a summon timer, like an orb
of destruction).

Now only dismiss forbidden allies, and reliably dismiss all of them.
Remove a no longer used prop key

Don't swap-push allies onto traps

Normally, moving onto an ally's tile swaps them with the player's current
tile, but if that isn't possible for some reason (often because the ally
cannot survive where the player is standing), they are pushed to a random
adjacent space instead.

This didn't check for traps and could unexpectedly trigger them, despite
friendly monsters otherwise refusing to step on them.

This isn't a scenario which previously happened very often (since it
required specific terrain), but the crystals that follow jademantle at all
times have this swap behavior by default and would trigger traps as you
walked by them for no 'obvious' reason.

(This change does make it very, very slightly more likely to get 'stuck'
over water with zombies crowding the shoreline, but in those cases the
player probably still didn't want to trigger an alarm trap unexpectedly.)

New tile for the Shapeshifter background

Made by regret-index, modifying aidanholm's generic monster spell icon.

Place only decorative clouds at the destination of attracted monsters

The tloc cloud at the arrival point of a monster affected by !attraction
(or attractitis) was explicitly only added to make the effect more
noticable, but had the awkward property of preventing mistmane's vapourise
effect from placing clouds beneath any attracted monsters.

Remove this heavy antisynergy by making the destination cloud purely
decorative, so it can be overwritten.

Make mutagenic clouds inflict damage/explosions to monsters

Instead of doing nothing at all to monsters, standing inside a mutagenic
cloud now builds up contamination over time (similar to flux form's melee).
When it reaches 3 stacks, the monster takes some immediate damage and
causes a 3x3 explosion around themselves.

This better-mirrors the effect of contamination on the player (not that
this is an intrinsic good), but in particular allows mutagenic cloud spray
from mistmane form to be an interesting form of offense. (And the idea of
actively encouraging mid-combat !mutation quaffing is deeply amusing to
me.)

The explosion *can* damage the player, but the timing of clouds applying to
monsters also means that the player can fairly reliably step away at 2
stacks and leave them to explode on other things.

One slight oddness is that by sharing the status effect with flux form's,
whether the contamination causes an explosion or not depends on whether
the cloud or a melee attack gets the last word. I think this is probably
fine, though.

Another concern is that these clouds becoming harmful to monsters may
disrupt some vault uses, but the vault where this looks more prominent
was already using ugly things for their immunity to the malmutate
side-effect, so I have given them immunity to mutation clouds as well.
Hopefully there will be no other major problems caused by this.

Don't cover interesting features with corpses

Corpses were large enough that they could sometimes almost entirely hide a
trap beneath them. Since they are purely decorative now, simply don't draw
them on top of any more important features.

Also, don't show an item stack indicator if all of the items in the stack
are also corpses (to avoid the player ever considering examining that tile
to see what the additional items might be - especially if on a staircase,
which hides all items.)

Allow examining more features when xv-ing a tile with an item on it

Only traps and stairs/altars/portals would show up on the xv menu if a tile
had an item in it, but this excludes multiple features with actual effects.
Be slightly more expansive about 'interesting' features.

(Some of these are still low-impact or decorative, but I feel like the
criteria for 'trying to examine this specific square' should be a lot
looser than 'what shows up on ctrl+x', which is why this does not use
is_terrain_interesting())

Run final effects after each fsim round

The lack of this was preventing things like Jinxbite or spectral weapons
from being processed properly (which resulted in some very incorrect and
confusing output, where it would look like the *player* was taking massive
damage from something?)

(When I checked to see if this caused issues with fsimming monsters with
other fineff-handled effects, I found that exploders and starcursed
masses crashed, but it appears they already did that before this commit,
so hopefully this is at least a status quo improvement)

*Actually* generate job groups on the charater creation screen from yaml

6925c6b set up much of the infrastructure to do this, but the header file
it generated was never actually used. (And if it *had* been used, it would
have crashed, since the menu coordinates it provided for the job groups was
very incorrect and couldn't dynamically adjust to how many jobs were in a
given category.)

This commit fixes that oversight and allows the vertical position of job
groups to also be generated automatically. You are only required to specify
the column number in job-gen.py and it will automatically adjust based on
how many jobs are in each prior group in that column.

Remove the 'width' member of job_group and species_group

As far as I can tell, this has been unused for ~7 years, since the UI
framework used to generate these menus was changed.
Move all talisman backgrounds into a new job category, 'Metamorph'

New background: Stalker

This is a stabbing-focused shapeshifting background, providing a suite
of non-spellcasting-related tools that help with stealth and provide
stabbing opportunities in an almost entirely non-overlapping way with
Enchanter.

It starts with a +1 dagger, a hypnotic talisman, mist talisman, 3
centipede baubles to give an offensive payoff for shapeshifting skill
before the mist talisman becomes usable, and 3 potions of attraction
(which have some synergy with mistmane form and might even in rare cases
be useable before then - or at the very least, provide players with some
easy opportunity to experiment).

While it doesn't have D:1 emergency consumable like Enchanter's potions
of invisibility, hypnogecko's tail drop is its own sort of emergency
consumable (and the form provides slightly better baseline stats for
your gameplan).

Add Centipede baubles

Intended as starting Stalker consumable, this is an experiment with doing
something very different than a full temporary form with a bauble.

Using one of these temporarily replaces your weapon with a reach 2 short
blade that has venomous side-effects. Its plusses (and the power of its
poison, which can eventually slow or even briefly paralyse) increase with
shapeshifting skill.

It lasts for a limited number of attacks, after which the centipede has
grown enough to pull free of the player's body and fight as an independent
ally for a short while.

No actual melding is involed (melding an individual weapon slot while
allowing the player to wield a different weapon sounds very technically
difficult), but instead, whatever weapon the player was wielding before
using the bauble will be automatically re-equipped if the player still has
it. This weapon-swapping is instant (even for Coglins).

It isn't usable with starting shapeshifting skill (so that the player
doesn't activate it immediately), but is intended to somewhat bridge their
two talismans and be a new type of combat consumable.

(I also think this 'temporary weapon' code has potential for numerous
future uses as well.)

-------------------------------------

The tiles were made by regret-index, using the following tiles:

 * Bauble: A CC0 gem made by Surt, and an unused coiled taipan submitted
   by LemurRobot.
 * Player doll: An unused sacred scourge tile by roctavian and an unused
   dagger for the Enchantress by Poor_Yurik.
 * Centipede: Denzi's old giant centipede tile.

Add item_def::summoned() to replace direct ISFLAG_SUMMONED checks

Similar to ::cursed() and very slightly more concise. (And will be used
several more times in a following commit.)

New tier 2 form: Mistmane

Intended as Stalker's capstone form, this form transforms the player's
head into a billowing cloud of mist. Intended as a homage to the
long-removed Evaporate spell, it allows the player to metabolise potions
into sprays of harmful clouds that help them stab their enemies.

While in this form, any potion the player drinks will temporarily give
them the Vapourise status, causing their next melee attack (whether it
hits or not) to spray a 3-tile wide beam of clouds in the direction of
the attack. The type of cloud created depends on the potion consumed:

!curing and !mist: Blinding Haze
!berserk rage: Fire
!mutation: Mutagenic Fog
All other potions: Noxious Fumes

The most common potions provide a baseline effect that is somewhat
comparable to Gloom, while more dangerous potions offer potentially
powerful direct damage as well.

In addition, while in this form, the player passively creates potions of
mist as they explore the dungeon. While these potions have only minimal
benefits on their own, they provide dependable baseline access to clouds
that isn't contingent on loot RNG. (Any mist potions in the player's
inventory will be destroyed whenever they take off the talisman, meaning
there is never any incentive to 'farm' them for future use. They are
solely a perk of the form itself.)

As a trade-off for access to so much quiet cloud generation, melding
away most of your vocal apparatus makes spellcasting much more
difficult, halving all spellcasting speed. In some ways, this form is
intended to provide an 'alternate path' for direct stabbing distinct
from hexes, so this makes it a bit less likely one will pick up hexes
alongside it. And because you are less incentivized to train magic
skills while levelling, your 'off-roads' from your starting kit are
likely to be different as well, potentially branching into forms like
werewolf or even vampire.

(The form also melds your helmet, but provides blindness immunity,
allowing the player to freely move within their own blinding haze.)

-----------------------

The mistmane form and talisman tiles were made by regret-index, using
the following tiles:

* Talisman: A CC0 potion by IdylWild and Denzi's old Scimitar of Flaming
  Death tile.
* Form tiles: Ontoclasm's scroll of fog icon.
 * Octopode: Sastreii's statue octopode tile.
 * Felid: One of Denzi's base felid tiles.

New cloud type: Blinding Haze

These clouds have an HD-based chance of dazing creatures standing in them
(somewhat less generous than meph's at high HD).

Intended to be used by Mistmane form, but may have other future uses as
well.

----------------------

Cloud tile made by regret-index, using Ontoclasm's seething chaos clouds.

Add potions of Mist (for upcoming Mistmane form)

These potions do not generate normally (and should not be placed by
vaults), but are intended to be generated passively by Mistmane form.

They temporarily make the player insubstantial, providing all the
resistances that implies (and immediately breaking the player out of
active constriction effects, shaking off sticky flame, etc.)

(Of course, since the potion fungus mutation exists, I also had to
implement a monster version of this status effect.)

-------------------

Potion icon made by regret-index, using Ontoclasm's potion of haste and
scroll of fog icons.

Hide never-droppable items in the drop menu

And don't suggest (d)rop as an action when examining the item.

(Currently this is only for installed gizmos, but a few other non-droppable
items will be added in a subsequent commit.)

Don't refuse to land player in harmless clouds via teleport/revival

All tiles containing clouds were vetoed as destinations for teleport (and
felid revival). This included harmless clouds like fog and also completely
decorative clouds like magical condensation.

While this did allow some niche strategies like reading ?fog prior to ?tele
to improve your odds of not landing nearby, this behavior is also extremely
undocumented and a little silly (and also prevents teleporting into parts
of several harmless vaults that use decorative fog or mist).

Instead, only ban the player from landing in *harmful* clouds.

New tier 1 form: Hypnogecko

Intended as the starting form of the revived Stalker background, this
form emphasises stealthy play while offering a unique defensive cooldown
for the early game.

Like real life geckos, this form can shed its tail as a distraction when
threatened. Unlike real life geckos, this distraction is literally
hypnotic, forcing monsters to pay attention to the shed tail instead of
the player. Triggered whenever the player is reduced to 40% of their max
HP, this trait causes the player to take a free step backward and leave
their shed tail wherever they were previously standing. The tail has
fairly low HP, but fast regeneration, making it extremely durable
against monsters at the start of the game in particular, and compels any
nearby monsters to prioritize attacking it instead of you (though they
will still be happy to hit you if you stand in their way!)

The player can use this distraction to either escape and reset a fight
*or* to get in guaranteed distraction stabs and possibly end the fight
outright. The form even provides a small bonus to the chance of
distraction stabs succeeding, to assist with that.

The tail will eventually regrow, but regenerates not with time spent,
but with exploration. I felt this was more appropriate and interesting
for a stealthy starting form than an XP-based cooldown, since you may
sometimes not be in a position to directly kill many things at all in
the extreme earlygame (especially with your tail already gone), and it
promotes sneaking around instead.

The form also provides a passive stealth bonus and a tiny amount of
regen (1/4th of a pip), but melds gloves, boots, barding, and body
armour.

I feel it provides an interesting earlygame 'consumable' (as a distinct
alternate to Enchanter's potions of invisibility) that also comes with
some unique positional implications: for instance, the player may want
to try fighting potentially dangerous battles in a position where - if
their tail were to fall off - they would still be able to reach their
attackers to stab them without body-blocking their own tail. I hope
players find it similarly fun.

-------------------

The hypnogecko tiles were made by regret-index, using the following
graphics:

 * Talisman: A CC0 tentacle item made by 7Soul1.
 * Forms: Sastreii's draconian player doll tile and Denzi's
   human player doll tiles.
  * Other species: Denzi's centaur / felid player dolls and old
    giant / leopard gecko tiles, ontoclasm's gargoyle player doll tile,
    Bloax's octopode player doll tile, Sastreii's naga player doll and
    statue Djinn form tiles, and LemurRobot's coglin player doll tile.
 * Tails: Denzi's old anaconda tile + an April staff by CanofWorms.

New background: Mystic

This is a magic-using shapeshifter background with spells that draw from
each of Earth, Air, Fire, and Ice magic (including the game's first
4-school spell), as well as talismans to support this.

The wide spread of schools is intended to allow a diversity of off-roads
without railroading players towards any one in particular. Their kit
makes use of many terrain manipulation effects and a uniquely 'mobile'
playstyle, where you are incentivized to actually move back and forth
between pickups on the battlefield, with their starting talisman
covering for how it takes longer for a bread-and-butter spell above
level 1 to come online. Giving more reason for mages to train early
shapeshifting hopefully also provides new incentive for mages to engage
with talismans earlier on.

They start with the spells Ice Thorns, Sirocco, and Dragon Veins, as
well as a robe, potion of magic, and vision and jademantle talismans.

New level 2 Air/Fire spell: Sirocco

Intended for the Mystic starting book, this spell is a range 1, 3-wide
'fan' that inflicts a modest amount of 50% resistible fire damage and
also pushes away damaged targets several spaces. To prevent it from
being a trivial kiting tool at low levels, the damaged monsters are
given brief swiftness and the spell has a short cooldown which doesn't
progress on turns the player moves.

This might sound somewhat heavy-handed, but the intent is that the spell
be used to create a few turns of 'breathing space' rather than a proper
escape - it synergizes with Ice Thorns, pushing monsters over leftover
thorns they hadn't yet walked on, as well as giving the player time to
pick up glimmer clouds without simply making the former spell obsolete.
It also can help sometimes with Dragon Veins usage, moving a monster
aside so that the player can step on one of the remaining veins. It also
provides a gap-filling option in areas where Ice Thorns isn't usable,
and maybe buys enough time to reposition where it is.

----------------------

The Sirocco spell icon and effects were made by regret-index, using
CC0 spell icons by Frosty_Rabbid and 7Soul1.

New level 1 Ice/Earth spell: Ice Thorns

Intended for the Mystic background, this spell creates a ring of ice
thorns on the ground around a targeted monster. These thorns do a small
amount of ice damage (50% resistible by rC) to any creature but the
caster who steps on them, then disappear. If the caster steps onto them,
they will be destroyed harmlessly and flying creatures do not interact
with them at all.

This spell provides a full-LoS that synergizes smoothly with Vision
form, allowing the player to stockpile glimmer clouds as monsters
approach, then collect them to kill any monsters that survive the
approach (and also allow them to deal with flying enemies). It is also
distinct from the many projectile spells which fill out the level 1
options for other backgrounds.

--------------------

Tiles made by regret-index, using various CC0 JRPG map pieces by
finalbossblues and Denzi's old bolt trap tile. The ice dust tiles they
leave behind combine ontoclasm's foxfire trail clouds with Denzi's grey
smoke clouds.

Don't claim plurally-named projectiles 'does no damage'

Allow setting bolt.plural to make it say 'do no damage' instead.

Remove some effectively-obsolete code regarding god-angering beams

This code was barely used anymore, and the player should already be
prevented from using effects that are innately objectionable to their god.

Fix some non-damaging beams saying 'but does no damage' against monsters.

Most cases were already handled for such attacks hitting the player, but
not monsters.

Add a power member to map_terrain_change_marker

To store spellpower information for some terrain changes (eg: allowing
damaging terrain to scale with spellpower).

Slated to be used in a subsequent commit.

New level 3 Air/Earth/Fire/Ice spell: Dragon Veins

Crawl's first 4-school spell, intended as the capstone spell of the
Mystic background. It allows the caster to tap into leylines of
elemental power, providing efficient and flexible multi-target damage,
with unique positional requirements.

Casting it creates 4 'dragon vein' features adjacent to the player in a
fixed configuration: Air above, Earth below, Fire to the left, and Ice
to the right. Stepping onto one of these dragon veins consumes 1 MP to
channel an immediate destructive effect against up to 3 targets, each
with different targeting properties and secondary effect:

Fire: Inflicts fire damage on the 3 monsters with the least health.
      Leaves behind brief fire clouds on any it kills.
Ice: Inflicts cold damage on the 3 monsters with the most health.
     Briefly freezes them, slowing their movement.
Air: Inflicts irresistible damage on the 3 most distant monsters.
     Does less damage, but suffers no falloff with distance.
Earth: Inflicts seismic damage on the 2 closest monsters.
       Stuns those within 2 tiles of the player for a turn.

Aside from Air, all do reduced damage to targets more than 3 tiles away.

The fixed positioning makes it easier for the player to remember what
goes where, and also has interesting effects in confined spaces - for
instance, only fire and ice are available in horizontal corridors
whereas only air and earth are available in horizontal ones. The player
needs to balance which effect is most desirable at the current moment
with which position they would rather be standing in.

These dragon veins can only be created on dry floor, but triggering them
counts as casting a spell for the purposes of many effects (such as
Vision form, but also spellclaws and battlesphere), and since glimmer
clouds can stack on top of features, the player can sometimes move
around triggering both things at once. The player can trigger 2
different dragon veins before the spell ends.

It may be an unusually involved spell, but I feel the effects become
quite intuitive in practice and it fits both the Eastern mysticism
themes of the background as well as its mechanical themes of movement
and terrain effects. I hope people find it fun, too.

-----------------------------

The Dragon Vein tiles were made by regret-index, using CC0 shield trim by
SnoopethDuckDuck and a CC0 crevice by FinalBossBlues.

Don't claim that enemies are being 'targeted' by your firewood on xv

No matter how much that block of ice wishes it could hurt something, it
cannot.

New tier 2 form: Jademantle

Intended as Mystic's capstone talisman, this form synergizes with elemental
magic in a unique way and offers some unusual defensive benefits.

While in this form, the player is flanked by 4 elemental crystals on the
diagonals - one each for Air, Earth, Fire, and Ice. These crystals can
wall-walk and try to stay in a fixed configuration around the player
(barring any monsters getting in their way). Whenever the player casts a
spell matching one of those schools, a corresponding crystal with enemies
near it will become charged, dealing damage to multiple enemies within
a range of 3 around itself and starting to glow with elemental energy.

If the player charges all 4 crystals at once, they gain a temporary
Resistance buff and a small amount of Indomitable, as a minor additional
reward.

The crystals reconstitute themselves a short while after they are
destroyed (whether by you or an enemy), also providing a form of passive
defense on top of this.

In addition, the form provides +2 skill to all elemental schools, but
reduces other magic schools by 1/3rd, melds helmet and cloak, and leaves
the player vulnerable to LRD.

---------------------------

The jade mantle form and talisman tiles were made by regret-index, using
the following graphics:

* Talisman: Denzi's old orange crystal statue tile, plus multiple CC0 earth
  spell icons by 7Soul1.
* Form tile: Further CC0 earth spell icons by 7Soul1 and Sastreii's
  shattered gem tiles.
  * Felids: CanofWorms' and LemurRobot's vampire felid form tile,
    Sastreii's current felid death form tile, and the above earth +
    gem pieces.
* Crystals: Further CC0 spell icons by 7Soul1, CC0 spellbooks by Shade,
  roctavian's spriggan air mage tile, and Sastreii's walking frostbound
  tome + salamander fireband tiles.
* Charge VFX: Denzi's default generic damage vfx tiles.

New tier 1 form: Vision

Intended as the starting form for the upcoming Mystic background, this
talisman opens your third eye, allowing you to see the remnants of cast
spells and turn them against your enemies.

Whenever you (or a nearby enemy!) casts a spell, it creates a cloud of
glimmer on a nearby tile. Stepping onto one of these clouds consumes it
to fire a small magical projectile at a nearby enemy you have line of
fire to. Enemies stepping on these clouds displace them to an adjacent
tile (and so do you, if there's nothing to shoot at).

This creates an interesting dynamic where low level spells provide more
efficient damage, allowing Mystic to deal with threats their initial
spells would be insufficient to handle, but require the player to move
in unusual ways to do so.

The form also gives sInv and +3 int, but melds gloves and helmet and
lowers your HP by 10%.

-----------------------

The vision form and talisman tiles were made by regret-index, using the
following graphics:

* Talisman: One of Denzi's old amulet tiles.
* Forms: A rejected Ashenzari altar tile by roctavian.
  * Vision felids: Two of Denzi's current base felid tiles.
* Glimmer motes: Sastreii's blastmotes cloud tiles.

Try to reduce information leaks from friendly wall monsters

Since wall monsters can be seen from either side of a given wall, they can
be attacked by monsters who are on the opposite side of the wall from the
player who summoned them. The player still sees what is happening to them,
though, meaning that they can be reliably used to determine the presence
of awake monsters on the other side of that wall (potentially inside a room
with a closed door) from complete safety by waiting to see if anything
attacks them.

It's somewhat hard for the player to reliably gain a wall-walking ally at
the moment, but that is slated to change, which will make this problem a
lot more important.

This uses a fairly crude check to prevent hostile monsters from targeting
or attacking friendly wall monster from the 'other side' of that wall by
checking that the attacker can set the player's cell. This has false
positives with corners, but it doesn't seem terribly important if enemies
too far away to be seen can't attack your wall monsters, even from the
'correct' side of the wall (and far less important than what this is
preventing).

Draw status lights in the same order in webtiles as in other versions

Local tiles and console defined a 'priority order' for status lights on the
HUD, vaguely trying to put more important ones first. Webtiles ignored this
list entirely and printed them purely in enum order.

This commit adds a status_iterator that can be used to iterate through all
statuses in a standard order (no matter where we are doing this) and syncs
webtiles with the other versions of the game.

Now, the exact ordering used could possibly use a little review or
updating, but 'incomplete priority list' is surely better than enum order.

Allow multi-coloured status lights

Instead of being forced to colour an entire status light a single colour,
it is now possible to use colour tags within it to colour each character
arbitrarily.

To do this, set inf.light_text_formatted to whatever one wishes, eg:
 "<red>T<green>e<blue>s<magenta>t"

Note: inf.light_text should still be set to the unformatted string in this
case, since that is used for status tooltip lookup in webtiles.

(I believe this should be used sparringly, but there are a couple cases
where incremental colouring as a sort of 'progress bar' might be helpful
UI)

Fix item gen treating Maw and Blade talismans as a tier lower than they are

When these forms were adjusted in 0.34 (and moved up a tier), the place
that controlled item generation didn't get the memo (which made them more
common early and less common late than other talismans of their tier, and
also affected acquirement's assessment of its suitability for your current
shapeshifting skill.)

Pull many monster post-cast effects into their own function, refactor

A number of effects that triggered upon a monster casting a spell (such as
battlesphere and orb of stardust) were only processed inside
handle_mon_spell() and not several other codepaths where monsters can be
made to cast spells.

Almost none of those mattered in practice, since none of the current
post-cast effects can apply in most of those cases (eg: your lightning
spire can't have an orb of stardust or a battlesphere or have its magic
Sapped), but one case that did theoretically matter was Dig (which is cast
in an ideosyncratic way by monsters).

So now, if somehow Jorgrun picks up an orb of stardust, it will work on
their dig spell.

(This doesn't matter much either, but it's useful future-proofing.)

Pull out some logic for post-spellcast effects into its own function

An increasing number of 'things triggered by casting a spell' were piling
up inside your_spells() and a pending spell will want access to these
side-effects without casting a spell manually.

This also allows Divine Exegesis to trigger spellmotor and spellclaws,
which was mostly an oversight. (Or rather, felt correct enough at the time
I implemented them, but I had neglected to notice that most other triggers
considered Exegesis a 'real' spellcast, so now these do also.)

Don't let ancestors set off blastmotes (rypofalem)

Allies normally refuse to step into blastmote clouds, to avoid exploding
them. But since ancestors are immune to all player damage, they assume
they are also immune to this clouds and don't avoid them.

And, well, they *are* immune to these clouds, but the player isn't and this
can blow them up in the player's face. So instead, put the blastmote check
*before* the check for cloud immunity.

If a non-piercing beam hits an actor, still draw the projectile on them

When non-piercing projectiles struck a target, they would not be drawn on
the target's tile. Unfortunately, this meant for spells cast at close
range, there would often be no indiciation that a spell was cast at all
unless it missed (including powerful things like Crystal Spear).

I hesitated on this one for a while, since 'seeing the projectile on top of
you' had gotten so strongly associated in my mind now (and probably other
people's) as 'the shot missed'. However, we have long-shown smite-targeted
vfx on top of targets they hit, so hopefully we'll just get used to it. If
not for history, it would seem very odd to hide the projectiles like this.

Remove an awkward hack involving bolt.path_taken

In order to ensure that bolt.path_taken was never empty after firing, if
the bolt really didn't go anywhere at all (usually because it was fired
directly at a wall), the source of the bolt was added to its path taken.

This is easy to observe by looking at the beam paths of any projectile
attack, if you aim it at a wall you're next to - the beam will appear to
hit the player instead.

This normally causes few problems since the tracer itself isn't fooled by
this (so you don't get prompted about hitting yourself). However, spell
autotargeting *was* fooled by this, and would assume that aiming at a wall
meant hitting yourself. Fortunately, aiming at a wall is also pointless, so
it was fine if autotargeting additional felt it was dangerous.

*However*, new multibeam spells will often have one or more of their beams
hit a wall, even while the other beams are doing productive things. But
autotargeting would incorrectly think that aim was unsafe, often preventing
it from aiming at monsters in confined spaces without force-casting. This
problem goes away if we stop claiming that it will affect a tile it won't.

However, the hack was put in place to stop a certain type of crash
resulting from assuming path_taken *must* be non-empty after fire() is
called. (see 1debe3e).

I have reviewed all current uses of path_taken carefully, and I believe all
remaining locations that assume the path is non-empty are correct in this
assumption (since they're aiming at a location that is already
known-reachable) and none of them can be reached by a player targeter. I
fixed some sign-related math in a few other cases this could potentially
cause an issue. *Hopefully*, this should be fine?

(This commit also incidentally improves the Wind Blast tracer very slightly
in the process.)

Add some convenience constructor for beams to reduce boilerplate

Bolts are constructed in hundreds of places in the codebase, and often
involve a lot of boilerplate for common idioms. This commit adds a handful
of new constructors that handle some of the most common cases:
 -A bolt for a spell or zap performed by a specific agent
 -A quick way to trace what open path exists between two spaces
 -VFX beams/explosions

It also refactor many existing uses to make use of these, generally making
things a fair bit more concise and removing superfluous code (a surprising
number of places defined agents and textual descriptions for entirely
visual beams with no mechanical effect...)

This is not intended to be exhaustive, and I mostly left alone any cases
that lacked a zap definition, did more bespoke things, or passed a beam
around between multiple functions to populate incrementally (of which there
is a lot).

(I also slightly tweaked the animations for Hailstorm and IMB while I was
editing them - to stop hiding the VFX when the former actually hits things
and to show the effect radius for IMB instead of looking like a weird kind
of sometimes-unidirectional spray)

Hopefully none of this has *added* bugs...

Don't even attempt to mesmerise players through grates/statues

Mesmerism immediately breaks when there are any solid features between the
player and the monster in question, though monsters weren't aware of this
and would use it anyway.

(This change doesn't actually stop merfolk avatars from trying, since their
song often has additional effects, but it feels like overkill for the
tracer to also check that there is water anywhere near them, just in case
you're somehow hiding behind a statue on completely dry land. Oh well.)

Change quicksilver bolt from ETC_RANDOM to ETC_MAGIC

Slightly more appropriate visual flavour, in my opinion. (Especially now
that its colour varies properly.)

Allow elemental colours to vary beam tiles per-cell

Elemental colour beams in tiles picked one random colour for the first
drawn cell and would repeat that same colour for every other part of that
beam or explosion. Instead, vary them per-cell like console does.

I believe this only affects quicksilver bolt, rimeblight explosions, chaos
breath and chain of chaos (the other elemental colour beams have bespoke
tile overrides) but will stop quicksilver bolt randomly looking like it's
made completely of poison or negative energy.

Don't override ETC_HOLY in tiles to only be yellow

It's odd that this was singled out in particular to ignore the colour's
normal meaning (and seems to date from a time when most elemental colours
were ignored in tiles entirely; see 3999269 )

Set beam attitude in bolt::set_agent()

I can't see a reason why we'd ever want the beam's atittude to disagree
with its initial agent (and if we do, we can still manually change it
later).

Not all places that use beams even currently properly set attitude (eg:
see 7f56f43) and I feel that at least a handful of places only do so
'by accident' (since a monster tracer separately sets attitude, and then
the beam is later reused). Nonetheless, this seems like 'correct'
behavior and hopefully won't cause any subtle issues.

Remove mons_attitude()

Completely identical to actor::attitude() (and often more verbose.)

Rename monster.attitude and monster.temp_attitude() to improve clarity

monster.attitude was a monster's true underlying attitude, while
temp_attitude() included effects like charm. This meant that
temp_attitude() returned 'the monster's current attitude in practice' and
was usually the one that should be queried for many effects.

Alas, the wrong one was used with some regularity, since it's easy to
assume that a monster's attitude is stored in the variable named
'attitude'. (It's also plausible to assume temp_attitude() means something
more transient than it does.). Recent commits fixed a slew of small bugs
resulting from using the wrong one, and many more have been fixed in past.

I am hoping that calling the underlying attitude member variable
'base_attitude' and renaming temp_attitude() to attitude() will make things
slightly clearer - and also make it more deliberate when one *does* use
base_attitude as opposed to attitude()

Correct a comment

I appear to have trailed off when I first wrote this....

Remove actor::real_attitude()

Used only rarely, and in almost all cases replacable by temp_attitude().

(We query a monster's real attitude directly all the time, but almost
always in a context where we know we have a monster, rather than a general
actor.)

Remove a never-functional property of Aphotic Marionette

Marionette sets a monster's underlying attitude directly, and attitude and
real_attitude() always agree with each other. So the willpower bypass here
would only work if the marionette was trying to hex a monster that was
*friendly* to the player (rather than the original intent).

This would be easy enough to fix, but, several years after their rework,
Dith has been doing just fine for themselves and I'm not sure that this
fairly opaque bonus to a handful of spells when marionetted is necessary.
They may be less effective on average than other options, but there's no
shortage of fantastic things to use it on already.

Fix a bunch of places incorrectly using monster base attitude

A handful of different places were using a monster's underlying attitude
rather than their current attitude (meaning they interacted incorrectly
with charm). This included:
 -Charmed nekomata still made hostile summons with Phantom Blitz
 -Malign Gateway cast by charmed monsters made hostile tentacles
 -Charmed monsters would walk into the player's own blastmotes
 -Seal Doors couldn't push charmed monsters out of doorways
 -spell_no_hostile_in_range considered charmed monsters to be valid targets
  for Anguish, even though the spell can't affect them

(And some other less consequential interactions.)

Also, remove an impressively obsolete comment while we're at it.

Don't prevent hostile ball lightning from blowing up at out-of-LoS targets

This check was only intended for friendly ones.

Also slightly simplify the player/monster target check of ball lightning
and seekers.

Slightly improve ally warning for Stomp

And don't have it treat charmed monsters as if they were fully hostile.

Remove a confusing exception to fedhas_passthrough()

Specifically preventing you from walking through hostile oklobs (but not
any other kind of hostile plant).

Encountering a hostile oklob while worshipping Fedhas already seems
impossible, but it's not clear what's different about them than any other
plant that can attack. (Almost certainly they were just the only
non-firewood plants that existed when this was first written.)

Remove some seemingly-unnecessary TRJ spawn code

copy_from_parent() should already take care of this on its own.

Simplify some monster speech code

This predates DESC_THE handling DESC_YOUR conversions for friendly monsters
automatically. (And I cannot figure out what rest of that block of code
could be doing that would be relevant; hopefully it isn't.)

Fix incorrect attitude of monsters charmed by charmed friendly monsters

If a friendly monster with a way to charm monsters was itself charmed by
a hostile monster (turning it hostile), any monsters that your former
ally charmed would still remain friendly.

ENCH_HEXED is supposed to mean (and is treated by much other code) as
'forced to be hostile' not 'forced to have the same attitude as what
hexed it'. (When friendly monsters charm other monsters, those get
ENCH_CHARMED instead.)

Add support for wide and starburst-like beams (of arbitrary size)

This commit provides a simple method to define, trace, and fire groups of
beams together at once.

'Wide' beams are all aimed in a single direction but have origin points
that extend to either side of the central beam. eg:

.****     ...**
@**** or  ..***
.****     .***.
          ***..
          @*...

while starburst-like beams are, well, like starburst (but can contain an
arbitrarily smaller number of 'spokes' and be aimed).

Both of these are limited to 8-directional aiming, for simplicty's sake
(which I hope can be an intuitive and interesting restriction upon such
spells.)

This multibeam implementation comes with a working player targeter.

Starburst has been refactored to use this implementation over its old code,
which allows each of the beams to animate extending outward simultaneously
instead of each beam fired fully in a random sequence. (It also probably
makes it simpler to make a monster version of this spell with a proper
tracer, though it's unclear how usable its AoE would be for a monster
anyway.)

Both of these new AoE shapes are planned to be used in multiple future
spells.

Refactor beam firing code to allow processing a single cell at a time

To be used in a subsequent commit to allow multiple beams to advance in
lockstep with each other - one tile at a time.

This commit also incidentally fixes a few minor bugs involving
affect_endpoint() not being called for beams that were stopped short for
a few reasons - such as to avoid allied monsters hitting the player with
them. eg: red draconian breath wouldn't leave a flame cloud anywhere, if
the player was on the other side of a monster that a friendly red draconian
was breathing on.

Translate status descriptions into Russian

Adds ru/status.txt and ru/monstatus.txt, 386 entries that had no
Russian at all. These are the short mechanical texts shown for player
and monster statuses, so they are read constantly and a wrong number
or a missing clause matters more than in flavour text.

The six Lua blocks are carried over structurally, with only their
strings translated. One of them, Water status, needed a different
shape: Russian takes a different preposition for deep water than for
shallow water, and the English keeps the preposition in the verb, so
the branches were rearranged to produce correct grammar. Dragon
status, which branches on draconian colour, is unchanged apart from
its strings.

All 20 [[...]] includes and both <blue> spans are preserved, and the
stat abbreviations AC, EV and SH are left in Latin so that the text
matches what the player sees in the status panel, which the game
renders from C++ and does not translate.

Restore missing Russian artefact descriptions

Twenty-seven entries in ru/unrand.txt had lost most of what the
English says, several of them down to a single phrase. The scimitar of
Flaming Death read only "It's smoking!", the sword of the Dread Knight
only "An indestructible long sword", Maxwell's patent armour only
"Odd-looking armour".

What went missing is usually the effect. The scimitar no longer said
that it sets opponents alight, the dagger of Chilly Death that it
slows them with ice, the morningstar "Eos" that it reveals invisible
creatures, the shield of Resistance what it resists, the robe of
Augmentation what it augments, the cloak of Starlight that it dazzles
onlookers, the robe of Clouds that it raises a storm.

Two said something the game does not. The partisan of Prune claimed
the curse acts slowly with no serious consequences, where the English
says an incapacitated wielder is certain to transform. The glaive of
the Guard had invented a different owner and a different story
altogether.

A few kept their flavour but dropped the hint that matters: the robe
of Misfortune no longer mentioned that its lucky colour has faded, and
the gauntlets of War no longer mentioned that the owner is destined to
die in battle.

Also fixes a stray double space in the obsidian axe entry.
